title: Eleven pills, three falls, a sleep aid
objective: Use the comprehensive geriatric assessment areas -- function, cognition, mood, falls, pain, polypharmacy, nutrition, senses, care preferences -- to individualize care
secondaryObjectives: Turn assessment data into a prioritized problem list, writing each problem as a NANDA-I diagnosis -- problem-focused, risk, health promotion or syndrome -- with the person's preferences in view

brief.situation: 21:00 on a medical unit. You are the RN for Mrs. Varga, 84, on day 2 of an admission for a heart failure exacerbation. She is on the standard heart failure order set. She asks for 'something to help me sleep', and the order set includes an as-needed diphenhydramine at bedtime.
handover: She lives alone, walks with a walker at home (not brought in), and wears glasses and hearing aids, which are at home.
Day shift charted her as 'pleasant, a little forgetful'. She has been up to the bathroom alone twice today.

Unit policy: the RN completes the geriatric screening areas within 24 hours for patients 75 and older, may hold an as-needed medication pending the provider when the screen flags a risk, and calls the provider and requests therapy, dietitian or pharmacy review on the findings.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What does Mrs. Varga's geriatric screen tell you, and how do you change her care tonight?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Polypharmacy with a benzodiazepine and an as-needed diphenhydramine (both on the Beers list), three falls, impaired cognition and attention, gait needing a walker, sensory loss without her aids, weight loss and low mood: high risk for falls and delirium.
parts.modelAnswer: Eleven meds including a benzodiazepine and diphenhydramine, three falls, she's forgetful and inattentive, can't walk safely without her walker, no glasses or hearing aids, losing weight and down. She's set up for a fall and delirium tonight.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Holds the diphenhydramine with sleep measures, arranges a walker, glasses and hearing aids with the bed low, calls the provider for a medication review and consults, and writes a prioritized problem list with her goal of going home.
parts.modelAnswer: Hold the diphenhydramine and use sleep measures, get her walker and have her aids brought in with the bed low, call for a med review and PT, dietitian and pharmacy, and write her problem list with her goal of going home.

scoring.modelReasoning: Geriatric assessment covers function, fall risk, medications, nutrition, vision, hearing, cognition, mood, toileting and goals of care. Mrs. Varga's screen shows polypharmacy with a benzodiazepine and diphenhydramine (both potentially inappropriate under the Beers criteria), three falls, impaired cognition and attention, unsafe gait without her walker, absent glasses and hearing aids, weight loss and low mood. Tonight: hold the sedating antihistamine, use sleep measures, give her the walker and aids with the bed low, call the provider for a medication review and therapy, dietitian and pharmacy consults, and write a prioritized problem list around her goal of staying in her own home.
